writtenTo: Philemon, a Christian slave owner in Colossae
importantNotes: Paul subtly undermines the institution of slavery by calling Onesimus a 'brother.'
Paul offers to pay Onesimus's debts — a picture of Christ's substitutionary work for us.
The letter shows how the gospel transforms social relationships from the inside out.
Onesimus means 'useful' — Paul makes a wordplay: 'formerly useless, now useful' (v. 11).
Church tradition says Onesimus later became the bishop of Ephesus.

chapters.1: Paul appeals to Philemon to receive Onesimus back as a brother, not a slave; Paul offers to pay any debt.
